name: Saints John and Paul
history: Two Roman martyrs named every day in the Roman Canon. Tradition holds they were brothers and Christian officials of the imperial household, put to death in their own house on the Caelian Hill under Julian the Apostate. A basilica was built over the house, and the rooms beneath it, with early Christian paintings, can still be seen.
life: The story of John and Paul comes down in a later account of their passion whose details cannot all be trusted, but their cult in Rome is very old and their names have stood in the Canon of the Mass since early times. According to that account, they had served Constantia, daughter of the Emperor Constantine, and when Julian, who abandoned the faith, came to the throne in 361, they refused to serve him or to offer incense to the gods. Given ten days to reconsider, they spent them giving away their goods to the poor. They were executed secretly in their house and buried there. In the late fourth century the senator Pammachius, a friend of Saint Jerome, built a church over the site. Excavations in the nineteenth century uncovered beneath it a Roman house with rooms painted with Christian scenes, including a figure at prayer.
prayerTo: Saints John and Paul, you were given ten days to deny Christ and you spent them giving to the poor. Pray for those who serve in public life, for brothers and sisters, and for households of faith. Make my home a place where Christ is loved, and my goods a gift to those in need. Amen.
penance: Give something you own to the poor today, an item or its value, as John and Paul did in their last days.
meditation: Their house became a church. What would it take for Christ to be truly at home in yours?
prayer: We beseech You, almighty God, that on this feast-day we may have the double joy of celebrating blessed John and Paul, true brothers who obtained eternal glory through one faith and one martyrdom. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
